title: Efforts to Streamline Social Service Offices' Processes to Ensure Timelier Renewals for ComCare Applications
what_it_is: Efforts to Streamline Social Service Offices' Processes to Ensure Timelier Renewals for ComCare Applications

sections.label: ComCare applications and home visits
sections.summary: ComCare Short-to-Medium-Term Assistance can be applied for online, and officers can make home visits to help home-bound applicants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development): Sir, through digitalisation, we have made ComCare applications simpler and more convenient especially for those who cannot easily leave their homes to apply for help.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: Applications for ComCare Short-to-Medium-Term Assistance can be made online on the SupportGoWhere portal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: Our officers can make home visits to assist those who still cannot apply online despite the guidance and are home-bound, such as the elderly or people with disabilities.

sections.label: ComCare Long Term Assistance renewals
sections.summary: ComCare Long Term Assistance is for persons permanently unable to work with little means, with longer renewal periods that let officers check wellbeing and needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: For persons who are permanently unable to work and have little or no financial means or family support, we can provide ComCare Long Term Assistance where the period between each renewal is longer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: The renewal process is still important as it serves as important touchpoints for our officers to check on our clients' wellbeing and identify any new needs.

sections.label: Balancing accountability and client check-ins
sections.summary: The renewal process is kept to ensure accountability for public money and to check on clients, though intervals can be extended based on merits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: And how might it improve the quality of life for some of these affected Singaporeans?

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: I think there is a need to strike a balance here: a balance between ensuring accountability because it is public money that we are dealing with, but perhaps a more important point is the need for us to check in on a regular basis with these clients.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: Because we do want to make sure that circumstances within the family have not quite deteriorated and if they have or if they have improved, what are the additional things that we can do to better support these clients.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: So, considering the two, I think there is a need for us to still ensure that this renewal process is in place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: But for cases where, based on their own merits, we can extend the interval for which each of this renewal is being carried out.
